paper.title_en: Quantum divisive hierarchical clustering based on Manhattan distance
paper.abstract_en: Classical divisive hierarchical clustering algorithms partition data by measuring similarities between data points and selecting the most distant ones to form clusters. However, their computational complexity is relatively high, and the time overhead becomes enormous as the data scale increases. To address this issue, this paper proposes a quantum divisive hierarchical clustering algorithm based on the Manhattan distance. First, an efficient Manhattan distance subroutine is constructed using the quantum Fourier transform and a probability amplitude interference mechanism, effectively avoiding the massive qubit consumption and deep circuit latency of traditional quantum adder trees. Meanwhile, to circumvent the uncertainty of Grover’s search algorithm, a quantum comparator is incorporated to achieve exponential acceleration in searching for the maximum distance between data points for cluster splitting. Based on these two core subroutines, a complete quantum divisive hierarchical clustering implementation framework is established. Finally, a time complexity analysis demonstrates that the algorithm reduces the O(N<sup loc="post">2</sup> d) complexity of a single iteration in the classical approach to O(N), exhibiting remarkable acceleration advantages for clustering tasks on large-scale, high-dimensional datasets.
